SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: Strong ester C=O Raman band at 1769 cm⁻¹ matches the expected ν(C=O) of a simple alkyl ester (≈1750-1780 cm⁻¹).  A very intense band at 901 cm⁻¹ together with a companion at 859 cm⁻¹ points to C–F stretching/CF bending modes, characteristic for molecules that contain a single –CH₂F/–CF moiety; only candidates 1, 4 and 8 contain fluorine.  Candidate 1 is an ester (methyl 2-fluoroacetate) so it fits the high carbonyl frequency, whereas 4 is a ketone (would give ν(C=O) ≈1715 cm⁻¹) and 8 is an acyl fluoride (would give ν(C=O) >1850 cm⁻¹).  Additional medium bands at 1192, 1255 and 1083 cm⁻¹ are consistent with C–O stretching of an ester and C–F/CH₂ wag modes expected for fluoroacetates.  The CH stretching region (2968, 2870 cm⁻¹) and CH₃ bend (1450 cm⁻¹) also agree with the presence of a methoxy group.  Overall, the experimental pattern best matches molecule 1: COC(=O)CF.
